C0.quote: identify necessary and sufficient conditions for social choice rules (SCRs) to be implementable
C0.note: Implementation of voting-type social choice rules on single-peaked domains; strategic aspects (strategy-proofness, Nash implementation).

C1.quote: an anonymous and unanimous SCR is implementable if and only if it is the median SCR
C1.note: Characterizations of implementable SCRs; implementability involves dominant strategy and Nash equilibrium requirements.

C2.1.value: preference profile; reported peaks; report of the state
C2.1.quote: Let P = (P1 , ..., Pn ) = (Pi , P−i ) denote a preference profile

C2.2.quote: P is the set of all strict, complete and transitive alignments over X
C2.2.note: Strict single-peaked preferences; in the mechanism agents report an alignment and a preference.

C2.3.quote: The preferences of agents are private knowledge, i.e. unknown to both other agents and the designer.

C2.4.note: Messages are separate from true state; the mechanism has a message space and truthful reporting is an equilibrium condition.

C3.1.quote: dominant strategy implementation ensures that the private preferences are also reported truthfully.
C3.1.note: Implementation analysis considers misreports of both alignment and preferences.

C4.1.note: Only ordinal preferences; no utility, welfare or satisfaction notions for voters are used.

C5.1.note: Unanimity and anonymity are normative axioms but not welfare, efficiency, representation or proportionality criteria; no evaluation by those criteria.

VOT.quote_behav: Nash implementation in the public component ensures nobody has an incentive to unilaterally misreport
VOT.quote_info: this alignment is common knowledge amongst the agents
VOT.note: Agents know the public alignment (common knowledge) but preferences are private; this is partial information.

ORG.note: The designer is a mechanism designer, not an organiser acting in the model.

DES.quote_info: with the designer uninformed of both
DES.note: Designer chooses the mechanism to implement an SCR; designer's objective is robustness to uncertainty. Designer is uninformed of the alignment and preferences, so info is NONE about them.

C7.1.note: Only VOT is an acting type besides the designer; with DES treated as present, both are STRAT, so C7.1 would be N. Rule: coded NA is not correct if two types present; revise: N.

C8.1.quote: requires Nash implementation in the public information and dominant strategy implementation

C8.2.quote: Nash implementation in the public information and dominant strategy implementation in the private information

claims.quote: The authority creating the committee would like to know what selection rules would be attractive
she should choose the median so that she can have this additional bulwark
she can identify which SCR she should choose from all of Moulin’s SCRs

C9.1.note: Claims about which rule the designer should use.

C9.2.quote: this alignment is common knowledge amongst the agents
C9.2.note: Needed assumptions (agents' strategic behaviour, common knowledge of alignment, private preferences, designer uncertainty) are all stated in the model.
